drhp.business: The Company operates three divisions - Cement, Sugar and Power. Cement is sold through a well developed network of dealers located in the states of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, some of whom have patronised the Company since inception. The Sugar Division crushes sugarcane and is seasonal in nature, its fortunes driven by cane availability, rainfall, irrigation and the zonal area allotted to the unit by the department, while the Power Division generates power and is constrained by state policy on the use of coal as an alternative fuel during the sugar off-season.
drhp.end_markets: Telangana|Andhra Pradesh|Dealer / trade channel for cement - the range of market operations for the cement product is restricted to the two Telugu states
drhp.expansion: The Company discloses no expansion programme. The MD&A 'Medium and long term strategy' section states that the range of market operations for the cement product is restricted to Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, that existing production capacity can be optimally utilised in catering to the requirements of the two Telugu states, and that consequently no medium and long term strategy is being envisaged in the absence of any immediate plans for expansion. The only asset-related intent stated is maintenance rather than growth capex: the Company endeavours to effect necessary changes and modifications …

litigation.note: The MD&A 'Opportunities and Threats' section states the Company will liaison with its legal advisers in respect of pending litigations concerning the power division, and will seek to resolve the complicated issues in the sugar and power divisions through negotiations with governmental authorities. Separately, the Directors' Report states there are no significant and material orders passed by the Regulators or Courts or Tribunals in the year under review impacting going-concern status. No case names, forums or amounts appear in the routed text.

risks.note: The MD&A states the range of market operations for the cement product is restricted to the two Telugu states and that existing capacity is sized to those states, so demand or pricing weakness in that single region has no offset elsewhere; the whole distribution model rests on one dealer network.
risks.risk: Geographic and market concentration - cement sold only in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh

risks.note: Management explicitly anticipates that variation in the prices of coal and other raw materials of the Cement Division could have some impact on performance in the current year, and can only respond by endeavouring to mitigate fixed overheads.
risks.risk: Coal and raw-material price volatility in the Cement Division

risks.note: The Government of Telangana has not been permitting power generators to use coal as an alternative fuel during the sugar off-season; management says that unless the Government revisits the issue it would be difficult for power generators to survive in the long run, as sub-optimal generation of power will seriously impact the viability of the industry.
risks.risk: State fuel policy makes the Power Division structurally unviable off-season

risks.note: The sugar industry is essentially seasonal; cane availability, good rainfall and proper irrigation determine its fortunes, and the zonal area allotted to the unit by the department governs how much cane can be sourced. Serious impediments in the Sugar Division cut crushing to 21,450 MT in the year under review from 47,887 MT in the preceding year.
risks.risk: Sugarcane availability, seasonality and zonal area allocation

risks.note: Fetching a remunerative price for sugar, adequate cane availability in close proximity to the plant, and industry-friendly governmental regulations are named as the key areas of concern for the division; cane price and incentives are set administratively rather than by the Company.

The MD&A says the Company will make its best endeavours to resolve the complicated issues in the sugar and power divisions through negotiations with governmental authorities and will liaison with legal advisers on pending litigations concerning the power division - outcomes are outside management's control and no timeline is given.
risks.risk: Pending litigation concerning the power division and dependence on negotiated outcomes with government

risks.note: Management frames its response to risk as effecting necessary changes and modifications to machinery and equipment and carrying out maintenance works to position the machinery in all divisions in robust condition so as to keep bottlenecks at bay, implying operational continuity depends on continual remediation.

The Company incurred a loss during the year, so no amounts were transferred to reserves, and it was not obliged to spend on CSR for FY2025-26 because it had incurred cash losses in the previous financial year - yet a dividend of Rs 3.00 per share was still recommended, an outflow funded from a loss-making year.
risks.risk: Sustained losses constraining the balance sheet
